lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the unusual stamens-opposite-petals + free-central placentation package, then route between superior-ovary Lysimachia and semi-inferior Samolus.

project_scope.selection_mode: Project module across Samolus and Lysimachia
project_scope.note: The four source rows represent three current species concepts because Samolus valerandi subsp. parviflorus is a synonym of accepted Samolus parviflorus.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: In a small 5-part fused flower, check whether the 5 stamens sit opposite the corolla lobes rather than alternating with them. Then inspect the one-chambered ovary for free-central placentation.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs in the local pool; leaves simple and exstipulate, with arrangement varying by genus.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Usually 5-merous and sympetalous; 5 epipetalous stamens characteristically opposite the corolla lobes. Ovary commonly unilocular with free-central placentation; superior in Lysimachia, semi-inferior in Samolus.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsule; dehiscence varies, including lid-opening/circumscissile in the pimpernel lineage and valvate in Samolus.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: LOOK HERE FIRST: in one flower, inspect five stamens opposite the five corolla lobes; confirm the free-central ovules in a one-chambered ovary when fruit is available. In Samolus, compare pedicel bracts and sterile stamens species by species: S. parviflorus has a minute bract near pedicel midpoint and five staminodes; S. ebracteatus has unbracted pedicels and NO staminodes. Staminodes are not a universal Samolus or Primulaceae requirement.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: stamens opposite petals → free-central placenta → ovary position → genus doors → duplicate-name cleanup
visual_lesson.intro: Primulaceae has a wonderfully specific flower-center clue: the stamens face the corolla lobes instead of sitting between them.

steps.title: 1 · Match each stamen to a petal lobe
steps.look_for: Five stamens positioned opposite the five corolla lobes.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the most teachable Primulaceae family characters.

steps.title: 2 · See the free-central placenta
steps.look_for: A central column bearing ovules inside a one-chambered ovary, not attached to the ovary wall.
steps.why_it_matters: Strong reproductive confirmation shared across the family.

steps.title: 3 · Lysimachia door
steps.look_for: Leafy annual with rotate 5-lobed flower, superior ovary and a capsule opening by a lid.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates scarlet pimpernel from semi-inferior Samolus.

steps.title: 4 · Samolus door
steps.photo_role: matched S. parviflorus / S. ebracteatus pedicel midpoints and dissected flower centers
steps.look_for: Small racemose flowers with a partly inferior ovary; first inspect the flower stalk (pedicel) for a bract. S. parviflorus has a minute bract near mid-pedicel and five staminodes; S. ebracteatus lacks both. These are species-level, not family-wide, characters.
steps.why_it_matters: Corrects the false shortcut that every Samolus flower has staminodes. Pair a pedicel macro with a dissected flower to distinguish the two local source-pool species.

steps.title: 5 · Collapse the duplicate Samolus row
steps.look_for: Samolus valerandi subsp. parviflorus → accepted Samolus parviflorus.

comparisons.title: Primulaceae vs Polemoniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both often have fused 5-lobed flowers with 5 stamens. Primulaceae places stamens opposite corolla lobes and has free-central placentation; Polemoniaceae has a 3-locular ovary and 3-valved capsule.

comparisons.title: Primulaceae vs Ericaceae
comparisons.rule: Primulaceae uses ordinary longitudinally opening anthers and the opposite-stamen/free-central-placenta package; Ericaceae commonly has poricidal anthers.

comparisons.title: Primulaceae versus Onagraceae at the flower base
comparisons.rule: Do not infer family from a floral tube alone. Local Samolus has a partly inferior ovary; many Onagraceae have a fully inferior ovary, while Lysimachia has a superior ovary. Confirm stamen positions and ovary/placenta structure before naming the family.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not teach ovary position as fixed across the project family: Lysimachia is superior, Samolus semi-inferior.

look_here_first: Locate one pedicel and inspect its middle for a minute bract.
Look inside an OPEN flower for five fertile stamens and, separately, five smaller sterile staminodes; do not infer absence from an undissected bud.
Check whole raceme peduncle: S. parviflorus usually very short (to ~0.7 cm in FNA); S. ebracteatus often 5–10 cm. Use multiple characters, not peduncle alone.
samolus_species_split.exceptions: The genus Samolus is variable for staminodes and pedicel bracts. The Primulaceae family-level clue is not the presence of staminodes.
samolus_species_split.reference: Flora of North America, Samolus key and species treatments (vol. 8), https://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242417215
